issue.title: Prune or archive hidden agent-artifact index rows: 4,706 of 6,775 rows are hidden and nothing ever removes them
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-k3.6 (land phase of epic sase-k3, ACE startup critical path); named as follow-up 3 in plans:202608/ace_startup_critical_path.md.

The agent-artifact index's 'hidden' flag is set on dismissal and hidden rows are never pruned short of a full rebuild. Re-counted on athena at master 1f388edee against the live ~/.sase state:

  sqlite3 ~/.sase/agent_artifact_index.sqlite
  agent_artifacts: total=6775  hidden=4706  (69.5% hidden)
  file size: 103.0 MB

The plan measured hidden rows accumulating at roughly 46/day, which is the mechanism by which ACE startup was getting worse every week.

Epic sase-k3 phase sase-k3.4 removed the read-path cost: ACE's Tier-1 startup and auto-refresh queries now use freshness='cached', which skips repair_stale_rows_for_query and per-row marker revalidation entirely, so hidden-row count no longer drives the syscall count on the startup query. That fixed the slope on the hot path but not the underlying growth.

Hidden rows still cost:
- the coalesced revalidating reconcile that sase-k3.4 left running after first paint (it stat-walks every row's artifact directory);
- the index's 103 MB on-disk footprint and its page-cache pressure;
- every remaining revalidating caller (bead pages, family attach candidates, agents/cli_index.py, agents_sync, sdd).

Scope: decide and implement a retention policy for hidden rows — prune outright, move to a cold/archive table, or age them out — including what still needs to resolve a dismissed agent by artifact dir, whether an existing rebuild path can serve as the recovery mechanism, and how the policy runs (lifecycle hook, maintenance chop, or an explicit command).

The index schema and query live in sase-core (crates/sase_core/src/agent_scan/index.rs); work there through /sase_repo (sase repo open sase-core) and read that repo's AGENTS.md first. Do not hand-edit the sase-core-rs pin in pyproject.toml.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-kg — the directory-mtime gate it proposes would make the background reconcile ~13x cheaper per row, which changes (but does not remove) the cost case for pruning. Whichever lands second should re-measure rather than assume this bead's stated reconcile cost.
